name: Guardian genius crossword No 229
preamble: All definitions are contained in the wordplay.

solutions.check: grid and clues read from the Guardian's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Two isles with numerous sheep

blocks.note: the Isle of Man plus I, the abbreviation for island or isle
a fold is a flock of sheep penned together

explanation.surface: A pair of Scottish or Irish islands teeming with grazing flocks.
explanation.walkthrough: As the preamble says, the definition sits inside the wordplay: 'numerous' reads as describing the sheep but defines MANIFOLD on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Manifold as an adjective means many and various, a literary synonym for numerous.

clue.text: Deliberate cruel treatment across central Uist

indicators.note: one thing lying across another straddles it, so the word for deliberate spans the other letters
central asks for only the middle of the following word to be kept

blocks.note: to muse is to deliberate, ponder
the two middle letters of the island name

explanation.surface: A deliberate act of cruelty committed somewhere in the Outer Hebrides.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is tucked between the verb and its container signal. Uist is an island in Scotland's Outer Hebrides.
explanation.definitionFit: Misuse is improper or harmful handling, which covers abuse or cruel treatment of a person or animal.

clue.text: Conclusions of Cern scientist: the show must go on

indicators.note: conclusions are endings, so only the final letter of each word that follows is kept

blocks.note: last letter of the laboratory name
the last letter of each of these five words

explanation.surface: Physicists at the CERN laboratory insist their experiments carry on regardless.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sits in the middle of the run of words whose endings are taken; it contributes no letter itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac Newton was the English physicist and mathematician who formulated the laws of motion and gravitation.

clue.text: Pack animal diagram up above fish tank initially

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the word is read from bottom to top
initially points to the first letter of the word before it

blocks.note: wolves hunt in packs
the char is a fish of the salmon family
first letter of tank

explanation.surface: A drawing of a llama or similar beast mounted over an aquarium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pack animal' suggests a beast of burden; here it is an animal that runs in packs. In a down clue 'above' simply places one piece before the next.
explanation.definitionFit: A flowchart is a type of diagram showing the steps of a process joined by arrows.

clue.text: IT's electrode kit for police interviews is faulty

indicators.note: something faulty is not in working order, so the letters are put into a different order

blocks.note: the letters of these two words, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: The IT department admits a component in the interview-room equipment is broken.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is wedged between the fodder and the anagram signal, reading like part of the sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Lie detectors, or polygraphs, are equipment some police forces use when questioning suspects.

clue.text: Horse and trap the Guardian essentially stabled

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so the middle letter is kept

blocks.note: a cob is a sturdy short-legged horse
a newspaper speaks of itself editorially as we
the middle letter of the seven-letter word

explanation.surface: A horse and its two-wheeled carriage kept in the newspaper's stables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse and trap' reads as a pony and cart, but trap is the definition. The Guardian, which publishes this puzzle, refers to itself as WE.
explanation.definitionFit: A spider's web is a snare built to catch flies and other insects.

clue.text: Back bit of window grille iron-clad

indicators.note: going back means the letters are read from right to left
a bit is only a piece, so the answer is a run of letters inside the words
the outer words clothe the answer, which sits within them

blocks.note: the run of letters from the end of the first word into the second

explanation.surface: A window protected by an iron grille fitted at the rear of a house.
explanation.definitionFit: An oriel is a bay window projecting from an upper storey, supported on brackets or corbels.

clue.text: Turn part of airway before one dons protective gear

indicators.note: to don is to put on clothing, so the letter goes inside the gear

blocks.note: to wind is to turn, as a handle or a road
the Roman numeral for one
personal protective equipment

explanation.surface: A worker sets the airflow before putting on their safety kit.
explanation.walkthrough: PPE, personal protective equipment, became familiar during the pandemic.
explanation.definitionFit: The windpipe, or trachea, is the tube carrying air from the throat to the lungs.

clue.text: Outlaw detective on robbery attempt

blocks.note: to outlaw something is to ban it
Detective Inspector
an attempt is a try

explanation.surface: A detective works on a case about a failed robbery by a fugitive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outlaw' looks like a noun for a bandit, which is tempting since BANDIT starts the answer; it is the verb for BAN, and the DI joins it.
explanation.definitionFit: Banditry is the activity of bandits, which is armed robbery and plunder.

clue.text: Noted surgeon drills with radius replaced by noon

indicators.note: one thing replaced by another means a letter is swapped out for a different one

blocks.note: to note something is to see it, past tense saw
to drill is to bore
r is the symbol for radius
N is an abbreviation for noon

explanation.surface: A famous surgeon practises drilling, with a bone of the forearm involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noted surgeon' reads as a famous doctor and 'radius' as the arm bone, but radius only supplies R, which N replaces in BORES.
explanation.definitionFit: Sawbones is old slang for a surgeon, from the days when amputation was a large part of the work.

clue.text: In Paris no American troops register for revolution

indicators.note: a revolution turns things round, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: the French word for no
GIs are US soldiers

explanation.surface: French refusal as American soldiers enlist to support an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For revolution' suggests troops joining a revolt; it simply turns the letters round.
explanation.definitionFit: To sign on is to enrol or register, as for unemployment benefit or a course.

clue.text: Amateur way card statuette made to move

indicators.note: the letters are made to move into new positions

blocks.note: A is a standard abbreviation for amateur
the two words as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An amateur's path to a statuette, as if card-playing could win a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sits inside the fodder, between 'card' and 'made', and gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Academy Award is the Oscar, the gold-plated statuette given for film achievement.

clue.text: Ordinary disciple overwhelmed by most of criticism

indicators.note: to be overwhelmed is to be engulfed, so one letter is swallowed by the others
most but not all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: O is an abbreviation for ordinary, as in O level
to take stick is to receive harsh criticism

explanation.surface: An ordinary follower crushed under a barrage of censure.
explanation.walkthrough: STICK loses its K to become STIC, which then wraps round O.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stoic is a follower of the philosophical school founded by Zeno of Citium.

clue.text: Cute play about trees put before institute

indicators.note: about suggests moving the letters around into another order

blocks.note: the letters of both words
I is an abbreviation for institute

explanation.surface: A charming drama about woodland staged ahead of an institute's event.
explanation.definitionFit: Eucalypti is a plural of eucalyptus, the Australian gum trees.

clue.text: One can't catch spy after preceding day's broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means put on air, so the words are judged by how they are spoken
after sends the piece before it to the second half of the answer

blocks.note: the eve is the day before, and the possessive matches the roof edge in speech
someone who cannot catch drops the ball

explanation.surface: A fielder who drops catches watches a spy after yesterday's broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are read in reverse clue order: 'after' puts the first piece second. The definition sits between them.
explanation.definitionFit: An eavesdropper listens secretly to others' conversations, which is a kind of spying.

clue.text: Winner oddly stored possession in gold vessel

indicators.note: oddly keeps the letters in odd-numbered positions
something stored is put away inside a container

blocks.note: the first part of OR, the heraldic word for gold, opens around the stored letters
first, third and fifth letters
the close of OR, heraldic gold
a ship is a vessel

explanation.surface: A champion kept their trophy inside a golden boat.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is gold in heraldry; the odd letters of 'Winner' are stored inside it, then SHIP follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Ownership is the state of possessing something, so possession is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Hendrix taking lead can be emulated atop counter

indicators.note: taking away the lead means the first letter is removed

blocks.note: Jimi Hendrix, the rock guitarist
a counter is a table or bench

explanation.surface: A guitarist's playing style can be copied by a player standing on a counter.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'atop' puts the first piece above the second. 'Taking lead' sounds like playing lead guitar.
explanation.definitionFit: Imitable means able to be imitated or copied, and to emulate is to imitate.

clue.text: Key dish everybody starts to order, perhaps

indicators.note: starts are beginnings, so the first letter of each following word is kept

blocks.note: the escape key on a computer keyboard
all means everybody
first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A crucial dish that everybody should order, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: Starts are taken from 'order' and 'perhaps' alike.
explanation.definitionFit: An escallop is a scallop, or a thin slice of meat (escalope), both served as a dish.

clue.text: Avoid poor communication by new team in shelter

indicators.note: something new is remade, so the letters take a fresh order
in places the reworked letters inside the following word

blocks.note: to miss is to avoid
first letter of TENT, a shelter, which opens around the reworked letters
the four letters reworked
the rest of TENT

explanation.surface: A new team camped in a tent should avoid communicating badly.
explanation.walkthrough: A TENT is a shelter; the rearranged TEAM goes inside it after the opening T.
explanation.definitionFit: A misstatement is an inaccurate or wrong statement, a failure of communication.

clue.text: Condition rodent to impregnate sloth

indicators.note: to impregnate is to enter and fill, so one word goes inside another

blocks.note: start of AI, the three-toed sloth, which opens around the condition
gout is a medical condition affecting the joints
close of AI, the three-toed sloth

explanation.surface: A disease spreading from a rodent into a sloth.
explanation.walkthrough: The AI, a three-toed sloth, is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: The agouti is a large burrowing rodent of Central and South America.

clue.text: Nervy women when monster on the rampage

indicators.note: a rampage is wild disorderly behaviour, so the letters are thrown out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
W is an abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: Anxious women when a monster is running wild.
explanation.definitionFit: A wyvern is a mythical winged dragon with two legs, found especially in heraldry.

clue.text: Very best rhubarb pastry eatery recalled

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the letters are read from the end

blocks.note: A1, first-class, with the 1 read as I
rhubarb is slang for nonsense, as is rot
a tart is a pastry

explanation.surface: Someone fondly remembers a restaurant's superb rhubarb tart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rhubarb pastry' looks like a dessert, but rhubarb means nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: A trattoria is an informal Italian restaurant, so an eatery.

clue.text: Unlikely to release drunk coppers

blocks.note: first meaning, completed by the last word: stingy, reluctant to let money go
second meaning: intoxicated
pennies, the small change a mean person holds on to

explanation.surface: The police are reluctant to let a drunk out of the cells.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition sits inside the first; coppers are pennies, not police.
explanation.definitionFit: Tight is informal both for mean with money and for being inebriated.

clue.text: Grand game afforded protection of port

indicators.note: something protected is surrounded and shielded, so a letter sits inside the other word

blocks.note: start of RUBY, a style of port wine, which opens around the letter
G is short for grand, a thousand
rest of RUBY

explanation.surface: A splendid match was given shelter in a harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruby port is a young, red, fortified wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Rugby is a ball game played by teams of fifteen or thirteen.

clue.text: Ask to keep guts of blue whale: accepted

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside
guts are innards, so only the middle letters are kept

blocks.note: start of BEG, to ask, which holds the middle letters
the inner two letters
end of BEG
A is an abbreviation for accepted

explanation.surface: A request to keep a blue whale's innards is granted.
explanation.definitionFit: The beluga is a small white Arctic whale, also called the white whale.

clue.text: Spooner's chaotic place fooled Mickey?

indicators.note: Rev Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words, so the sounds are exchanged

blocks.note: fooled is had, and Mickey is the cartoon mouse; swap their opening sounds

explanation.surface: A chaotic place where someone has fooled Mickey Mouse.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition again sits inside the wordplay, between the indicator and the words to be swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: A madhouse is a scene of uproar and confusion, from the old word for an asylum.

clue.text: Prince taxes those living abroad randomly

indicators.note: random order means the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: P is an abbreviation for prince
taken as written

explanation.surface: A prince haphazardly levies charges on people living overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: Expats, short for expatriates, are people who live outside their native country.

clue.text: Bill embracing alternative

blocks.note: an ad, or advertisement, is a bill
an option is an alternative

explanation.surface: A parliamentary bill that takes in an alternative proposal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Embracing' looks like a container signal, but it is the definition, placed between the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoption is the taking up of an idea or cause, which is what embracing it means.
